title: Predictive Gap Coalescer and KV Thin‑Striping for Mixed Prompt/Response SLOs
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Mixed prompt/response workloads (e.g., short user prompts followed by long assistant generations, or interleaved short/long turns) cause the continuous batching runtime to either fragment KV residency or to form suboptimal micro-batches that increase tail latency and GPU memory overhead. Existing heuristics favor latency (small-window flushes) which reduces batch token density and increases per-token cost, or favor throughput (long coalescing timers) which increases P95/P99 latency for short-turns.

Goal: Implement a scheduler + KV allocation strategy — the Predictive Gap Coalescer with KV Thin‑Striping — that increases token density while preserving latency SLOs for short-turn interactions and reducing GPU memory fragmentation for mixed-length workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) P95 latency for short-turn (<32 tokens) responses does not regress by more than 5% compared to baseline under representative traffic.
2) Average tokens-per-batch increases by >=12% on mixed workloads vs baseline.
3) GPU memory fragmentation metric (max slab free holes / total slab) reduces by >=20% during mixed-turn stress tests.
4) No customer-reported correctness regressions; rollout can be rolled back within 5 minutes.
success_metrics:
- P50/P95/P99 latency per request (short/long buckets).
- Tokens per effective batch (token density).
- KV hit rate and cold-kv miss ratio.
- GPU slab fragmentation score.
- Per-token cost estimate in staging benchmarks.
approach:
1) Predictive Gap Coalescer: compute a per-stream gap score that estimates the likelihood that the next N ms will include additional tokens from the same stream. Inputs: recent inter-arrival times, role-turn detection (prompt vs response), token production rate, and model-specific pacing profiles.

2) Soft-gap coalescing timers: rather than fixed coalesce window, use a dynamic soft timer that extends for high-probability gaps (small expected additional tokens) but caps extension based on a latency budget. If extension exceeds budget, force flush.

3) KV Thin‑Striping: when admitting contexts into KV slabs, spread high-churn short-turn contexts across more banks with smaller reservations (thin stripes) to reduce impact of eviction pressure on long-residency contexts. Long-residency contexts get denser allocation.

4) Idle Defrag Pass: schedule opportunistic GPU slab compaction during known micro-idle epochs (e.g., right after large batched responses) to reclaim fragmented space without impacting latency-critical flows.

5) Admission scoring and preemption: new admission score = f(token_density_gain, predicted_gap_probability, slot_tenure, kv_bank_pressure). Implement thresholding and preemption hooks that degrade gracefully (fallback to conservative coalescing) under high pressure.
experiments: A. Offline simulation with recorded mixed-turn traces (SRE trace corpus + synthetic mix): measure token density, latency per bucket, and slab fragmentation over 10M requests.

B. Staging canary (runtime build): 1% traffic routing for 24 hours with detailed tracing; compare P95 short-turn latency and cost to baseline. Link: https://dashboard.internal/runtime/canary/ENG-598321
C. A/B on dedicated cluster: 50/50 split for 6 hours with stress injection (90/10 short/long and 50/50 scenarios). Collect KV hit/miss breakdown and GC frequency.
D. GC/defrag safety test: force tight memory conditions and validate defrag pass latency impact and correctness under preemption.
E. Evaluation against adversarial churn workload to assert no pathological thrashing.
Note: experiment artifacts will be in the project Confluence and linked PRs.
rollout_plan:
Stage 1: Merge behind feature flag and e2e test coverage.
Stage 2: Staging canary (1%) for 24–48h, verify metrics and manual signoff.
Stage 3: Gradual ramp — 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 72h windows, with automatic rollback on any P95 short-turn latency > baseline + 7% or slab fragmentation > baseline + 15%.
Stage 4: Global rollout after 7 days of stable metrics.
Rollback: feature gate off; fall back to current coalescing timers and allocation policy.
risks:
- Overaggressive coalescing can increase P99 for very latency-sensitive short-turn customers.
- KV thin-striping could reduce locality and slightly increase cache miss rates for some workloads.
- Defrag passes introduce scheduling complexity and must not block critical inference threads.
- Cross-tenant interference in multi-tenant Dedicated customers if allocation heuristics misclassify tenant profiles.
mitigations:
- Conservative default thresholds; expose per-tenant coalescing policy via config.
- Gradual ramp with strict rollback thresholds.
- Add observability: new metrics for predicted_gap_accuracy, slot_preemptions, and kv_bank_pressure.
- Run closed-loop chaos tests in staging to observe regressions.
